decks.title: Amazoness Aggro
decks.description: Eleven Amazoness monsters and three Amazoness Village support an offense that replaces destroyed monsters. Amazoness Swords Woman turns unfavorable battles into damage to the opponent, while Amazoness Paladin and Amazoness Tiger benefit from having allies on the field.

guide.summary: Establish Village, trade monsters without losing field presence, and save removal for threats that prevent you from battling.
game_plan: Search for Amazoness Village with Terraforming and keep a second copy as a replacement; keeping the Field Spell active matters more than putting every Amazoness on the field.
Use the three Amazoness Paladin to apply pressure and the three Amazoness Swords Woman to punish large monsters. Village only replaces a monster once per turn.
Use Book of Moon and removal to open up specific battles. Keep resources in hand against Torrential Tribute or Mirror Force.
opening: With Village and an Amazoness, activate the Field Spell before committing the monster, and hold interaction so the opponent cannot easily remove both.
Without Village, Giant Rat or Warrior Lady of the Wasteland can set up your next monster. Reinforcement of the Army can find Swords Woman or Exiled Force depending on the field.
key_plays: Warrior Lady of the Wasteland recruits an EARTH Warrior with 1500 ATK or less: Swords Woman and Exiled Force are options. Giant Rat can also access Amazoness Tiger.
After an Amazoness is destroyed and reaches the GY, Village summons another of an equal or lower Level. A destroyed Swords Woman can leave the next one ready.
Amazoness Spellcaster swaps original ATK to overcome a boss monster. Amazoness Archers reduces ATK by 500 and forces the affected monsters to attack if able.
Amazoness Archer can Tribute two monsters to deal 1200 damage. Count that finishing option once the opponent is within range, after making any useful attacks.
pitfalls: Tiger is a Beast, and you can only control one. Warrior Lady of the Wasteland and Reinforcement of the Army cannot search for it.
Village requires destruction and a trip to the GY; banishing, returning a monster, or Tributing it does not trigger the replacement.
Do not declare Warrior with Tribe-Infecting Virus without counting your own Amazoness. Heavy Storm also destroys Village.
Amazoness Chain Master costs 1500 LP after being destroyed by battle; use the effect when the information and stolen monster justify the payment.

side_cards.reason: Against Chaos, Gozuki and graveyard-based Fusion decks, it applies pressure and stops the opponent from banishing cards from either graveyard. It does not stop Miracle Fusion or Dragon's Mirror from using only materials on the field. Two copies compensate for the lack of a searcher; the plans replace supporting cards while keeping at least nine Amazoness monsters.

side_cards.name: Cipher Soldier
side_cards.reason: Against Warrior and Amazoness decks, it wins battles without filling the deck with removal that feeds Village. As an EARTH Machine with 1350 ATK, it can be summoned by Giant Rat, but not searched by Wasteland or ROTA.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: An anti-burn monster that preserves the battle plan and Village. Its 1600 ATK means Giant Rat CANNOT summon it, even though it is an EARTH Beast. Two copies compensate for the lack of a searcher.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Protects important attacks and summons without negating Archers or your own defensive and revival traps. Two copies against traps; each costs 1000 LP and cannot answer the effects of traps that are already active.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado
side_cards.reason: Removes Decree, Skill Drain, Oppression and backrow without touching Village. Two copies handle persistent locks that Seven Tools cannot remove once they have resolved.

side_cards.name: Spell Shattering Arrow
side_cards.reason: Destroys opposing Field Spells, Future Fusion and Continuous Spells while preserving your own Village. Bring both copies only against decks with enough face-up Spell targets, not against backrow made entirely of traps.

side_cards.name: D.D. Warrior
side_cards.reason: A battle-based answer to a large or recurring boss monster. An EARTH Warrior with 1200 ATK, accessible through ROTA, Rat and Wasteland. This is a single toolbox option, distinct from the LIGHT D.D. Warrior Lady.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: One answer to set defenders and FLIP monsters that requires no battle and does not trigger battle recruiters. It preserves the Amazoness core without adding another Normal Summon.

side_cards.name: Bottomless Trap Hole
side_cards.reason: A second copy overall against large Warriors and monsters best dealt with by banishing. One extra copy avoids overloading on traps; it is not an answer to every monster summoned during the Damage Step.

side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Keep nine Amazoness monsters, all three Village and every recruiter. Rat can summon Cipher; ROTA, Rat and Wasteland can access D.D. Warrior. None of those cards makes Cipher a Warrior. Remove Tribe because declaring Warrior would also destroy your own board.

3 in, 3 out. Keep nine Amazoness monsters and every searcher. Kycoo stops the opponent from banishing from graveyards, not from the field or hand. D.D. Warrior removes a boss through battle, but also banishes itself and cannot trigger Village because it is not an Amazoness.

side_plans.matchup: Field Spells, Future Fusion and Continuous Spell engines
side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Arrow preserves Village while disrupting the opposing engine; Dust handles traps that Arrow cannot touch. Keep Enemy Controller and both Book of Moon as monster interaction.

side_plans.matchup: Burn / stall with Continuous Spells and Traps
side_plans.note: 8 in, 8 out, only after confirming a lock involving both Spells and Traps. Keep the entire Amazoness lineup, Village and its recruiters. Rat cannot summon Wombat; removing Ring and dead defensive cards reduces LP risk. Do not bring in Arrow without enough observed face-up targets.
3 in, 3 out. A small change to protect your pressure and remove a set wall. Keep ten Amazoness monsters; Tools protects a key attack without shutting off Archers or Call.

decks.title: Archfiend Pandemonium
decks.description: Three Archfiend General, three Pandemonium, and Terraforming provide access to the Field Spell that supports your Fiends. Archfiend Heiress and destruction by effects turn trades into new threats.

guide.summary: Keep Pandemonium active, apply pressure with efficient Fiends, and turn the destruction of your own Archfiends into searches.
game_plan: Discard Archfiend General to find Pandemonium when needed; once the Field Spell is established, you can keep other copies of General as attackers.
Start with Archfiend Soldier or Archfiend Heiress to enable Terrorking Archfiend later. That first monster also keeps you from relying on a single threat.
Use Pandemonium to find a lower-Level Archfiend after destruction by an effect; manage your Traps and LP to sustain this plan over several turns.
opening: General plus Terrorking: search for and activate Pandemonium, establish another Archfiend first, and save Terrorking for a later legal Summon.
With Heiress and protection, accept a battle trade that lets you search for the right Archfiend; do not spend removal just to preserve a small monster.
key_plays: Mist Archfiend can be Summoned without Tributing, attack, and destroy itself in the End Phase. With Pandemonium, that destruction lets you search for a lower-Level Archfiend.
Archfiend's Roar revives a threat for 500 LP and destroys it at the end of the turn; if Pandemonium is still active, that destruction can fuel another search.
Terrorking negates the effects of monsters it destroys by battle. Use it to attack effect-based engines when it can win the battle.
Desrook Archfiend in hand can bring back Terrorking when it is destroyed and sent to the GY.
pitfalls: Pandemonium removes the Archfiends' Standby Phase payments; it does not prevent Mist's 1000 damage or the 500 LP cost of Archfiend's Roar.
Terrorking cannot be Normal or Flip Summoned without another Archfiend on your field; Setting it does not make a later Flip Summon legal without that support.
Heiress searches when sent by an effect or destroyed by battle, not when discarded as the cost of Tribe-Infecting Virus.
The monster revived by Archfiend's Roar cannot be Tributed. If Pandemonium disappears, Archfiend General destroys itself; protect the Field Spell before relying on several copies.

side_cards.name: Dust Tornado

side_cards.reason: A transformation against Fusion, Dragon and Zombie decks. The plan removes Roar, Premature, Call and Desrook so your intended Special Summon lines are not left exposed to the opponent using Oppression.

side_plans.note: Mask shuts down the Tribute Summon line, Rug answers the summon-triggered effect, and Gemini Imps prevents Thestalos from turning the exchange into advantage.

side_plans.matchup: HERO Fusion / Red-Eyes / Dragon Future / Zombie
side_plans.note: Remove all four revival cards and Desrook, whose resolution outside the Damage Step could be negated by paying 800 LP. Kycoo blocks materials the opponent wants to banish from their graveyard, while Dust answers Future Fusion, Call of the Mummy and Continuous cards.
Kycoo prevents the opponent from banishing LIGHT and DARK monsters from their graveyard, while Dust removes Call, Premature or backrow without interfering with Pandemonium.

Virus destroys Spy in the hand or face-down, along with low-ATK engines, but a face-up Spy under Necrovalley has 1700 ATK and survives. After its initial resolution, it checks each draw until the end of the opponent's third turn; it does not continually inspect cards added by searches. Falling Down takes a face-up defender or boss while you keep an Archfiend on the field.
Falling Down takes the monster instead of merely destroying it, while Dust removes Village, Hunting Ground and set protection.

decks.title: Armed Dragon
decks.description: Three Flying Kamakiri #1 and three Masked Dragon provide access to Armed Dragon LV3. Three LV5, two LV7, and one Level Up! let you climb the chain, while Cyberdark Keel uses small Dragons in the GY.

guide.summary: Recruit LV3, reach LV5 with protection, and choose between evolving through battle or accelerating with Level Up!
game_plan: Use the six recruiters to survive and set up LV3, ideally during the opponent's turn so it can evolve in your next Standby Phase.
Save monsters with enough ATK for the effects of LV5 and LV7; do not automatically discard the only evolution piece in your hand.
Keep Cyberdark Keel's battle plan available while preparing Future Fusion and Dragon's Mirror as finishers.
opening: Set Masked Dragon or Flying Kamakiri #1 with protection. If it falls in battle, choose LV3 when it can survive until your Standby Phase.
With LV5 and Level Up!, first establish a legal LV5 and clear dangerous backrow before turning it into LV7.
key_plays: LV3 sends itself to the GY in your Standby Phase to summon LV5 from your hand or Deck. An LV5 that destroyed a monster by battle can summon LV7 during the End Phase.
Level Up! sends a face-up LV monster to the GY and summons the listed monster, ignoring its Summoning conditions; LV5 into LV7 is the highest-impact conversion.
When Normal Summoned, Cyberdark Keel equips a Level 3 or lower Dragon from the GY, such as LV3, Masked Dragon, or Twin-Headed Behemoth.
Future Fusion reveals Five-Headed Dragon and sends five Dragons during your first subsequent Standby Phase; Dragon's Mirror can then use those materials.
pitfalls: This list has only one Level Up!, not two. Preserve the natural evolution route and do not build every hand around drawing that copy.
Future Fusion does not load the GY on activation: it must survive until your first Standby Phase, and the Fusion arrives in the second.
Cyberdark Keel is a Machine: it is not Dragon material for Five-Headed Dragon and does not enable Stamping Destruction.
LV7 cannot simply be Summoned with two Tributes or Premature Burial. Sending Sinister Serpent for a LV effect only destroys monsters within its low ATK threshold.

Use Rug against Normal Summon-triggered effects. My Body only answers effects that destroy monsters, so it does not cover Thestalos or Mobius. Keep the recruiter core and all three LV5.

Remove the less useful summon responses and part of the delayed engine. Keep Mirror Force, Torrential Tribute, Ring of Destruction and Call of the Haunted; the cards brought in protect your development without negating those traps.

side_plans.note: Wombat does not make costs free. Against battle-focused Pyro, keep Mirror Force and remove a Future Fusion instead. The written plan assumes effect damage or a lock is the main threat.

decks.title: Chaos Control
decks.description: Two Chaos Sorcerer finish games for a core of six LIGHT monsters, useful DARK monsters, and defensive cards. Spy, Dekoichi, and Tsukuyomi sustain trades while both Attributes build up in the GY.

guide.summary: Trade patiently, reuse Flip Effects, and preserve LIGHT/DARK material so Chaos Sorcerer arrives with a specific job.
game_plan: Build the GY through useful battles and effects; do not needlessly sacrifice your six LIGHT monsters just to summon Chaos a turn earlier.
Protect Spy or Dekoichi when they can provide another card or a second monster, and use Tsukuyomi to reuse an effect when the field allows it.
Summon Chaos Sorcerer to remove a face-up threat or finish through attacks; count the fuel needed for the second copy.
opening: With Thunder Dragon, discard one copy to search for the other if it is still in the Deck. With only two copies, this is not a two-card search.
A Set Spy or Dekoichi plus protection lets you open without revealing Chaos. Against a known threat, ROTA can find D.D. Warrior Lady or Exiled Force.
key_plays: Book of Moon followed by Nobleman of Crossout removes a monster that was initially face-up, provided both effects can resolve.
Tsukuyomi can Set Spy or Dekoichi again for reuse on a later turn; it also turns an opposing boss into a target you can attack through its DEF.
Raigeki Break and Tribe-Infecting Virus turn a spare discard into interaction. Night Assailant can recover another Flip monster already in the GY.
Kycoo the Ghost Destroyer stops the opponent from banishing cards from the GYs while it is face-up, and can remove materials when it deals damage.
pitfalls: Chaos Sorcerer cannot attack in the turn it activates its banishing effect; do not count those 2300 when calculating lethal damage.
Night Assailant cannot recover itself. Sinister Serpent has a later banishing effect and does not guarantee endless discards.
Card Destruction can fix the opponent's hand and load their GY; use it for a concrete benefit, not just because it is available.
Nobleman on an opposing Spy can also banish your own copies of Spy from the Deck; assess the trade before resolving it.

5 in, 5 out. Wombat protects your LP, Dust breaks the lock, and Mirage protects only the Battle Phase. Heavy, MST and Raigeki Break remain for traps that are already active. Adding Mirage brings the LIGHT total to seven.

side_plans.matchup: Wall Rock / set defenders and backrow
side_plans.note: 4 in, 4 out. Use Crossout on set defenders, Dust on Weapon Change, Canyon and locks, and Mirage to prevent new battle trap activations. Do not apply this automatically in a Spy mirror; check which FLIP monster Crossout will banish from both Decks.

decks.title: Chaos Warrior
decks.description: Three Blade Knight, two Reflect Bounder, one D.D. Warrior Lady, and Ninja Grandmaster Sasuke supply the seven LIGHT monsters in this aggressive core. Warriors and removal clear the way for two Chaos Sorcerer without relying on a slow draw engine.

guide.summary: Win the early battles, force answers, and turn used LIGHT/DARK monsters into a second wave of Chaos.
game_plan: Present one protected attacker and keep the next in hand; Shrink and Book of Moon help win a battle without overextending.
Use Reinforcement of the Army to find the tool for the opposing field: Exiled Force, Mystic Swordsman LV2, or a useful LIGHT monster.
Use the two Chaos Sorcerer after your Warriors have drawn out removal and supplied both Attributes, without spending all the materials at once.
opening: Blade Knight plus protection applies pressure from the first turn. Do not empty your hand just to meet its conditions.
Against Set monsters, hold Mystic Swordsman LV2 or Nobleman of Crossout; against a face-up Defense Position monster, Ninja Grandmaster Sasuke offers another route.
key_plays: Shrink lets Don Zaloog win a battle and deal damage to activate its hand effect; it can also preserve your LIGHT monsters for another battle.
Book of Moon turns a monster face-down for Mystic Swordsman LV2 or Nobleman, each with its own activation timing.
Zombyra the Dark attacks over many early monsters; Book of Moon can reset its ATK losses when Setting it again is useful.
Chaos Sorcerer removes a face-up threat that battle cannot answer, while another Warrior remains available to attack.
pitfalls: Zombyra cannot attack directly and loses 200 ATK after destroying a monster by battle; calculate later battles using its current ATK.
Blade Knight only gains ATK with one card or fewer in hand, and only negates Flip Effects when its condition of controlling no other monsters is met.
The Main Deck's only Flip monster is one Night Assailant; discarding it does not produce a recovery on its own.
Do not cut the LIGHT package when siding without checking your access to Chaos. Sorcerer loses its attack for the turn if it uses its banishing effect.

decks.title: Dragon Future
decks.description: An entirely Dragon monster lineup supports three Totem Dragon, two Future Fusion, and two Dragon's Mirror. The list can win through ordinary pressure, evolve Horus, or finish with Five-Headed Dragon.

main_deck.name: Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV8
Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV6

thumbnail_strip: Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV8

guide.summary: Develop small Dragons, prepare a useful GY, and choose the boss that answers the field.
game_plan: Start with Masked Dragon, Luster Dragon, or Mirage Dragon; force the opponent to spend answers while Future Fusion prepares the next wave.
Keep Totem Dragon in the GY and your field empty when you want to revive it in your Standby Phase; it can count as two Tributes for a Dragon.
Choose Horus to control Spells or Five-Headed Dragon for ATK pressure. Save Dimension Fusion for enough banished monsters to justify 2000 LP.
opening: With Future Fusion and protection, activate the Continuous Spell early and protect the waiting turn; check that five Dragons remain in the Deck for its first Standby Phase.
Foolish Burial can send Totem Dragon if you plan to revive it in a later Standby Phase with an empty field, or a Dragon you need to recover with another card.
key_plays: Future Fusion loads five Dragons by revealing Five-Headed Dragon during your first subsequent Standby Phase. Dragon's Mirror turns field or GY materials into another Fusion.
Totem Dragon can count as two Tributes for Tyrant Dragon; a Totem revived by its own effect is banished when it leaves the field.
Horus the Black Flame Dragon LV6 can summon LV8 in the End Phase after destroying a monster by battle; LV8 lets you respond to Spell activations.
Mirage Dragon prevents the opponent from activating Traps during the Battle Phase; use it to support the decisive attack.
pitfalls: Future Fusion does not send materials on activation, and its Fusion is destroyed if the Continuous Spell leaves the field. Your own Heavy Storm can break that link.
Totem requires an empty field and no non-Dragon monsters in your GY; check that condition after bringing in monsters from the Side Deck.
Horus LV6 is unaffected by Spells, including your own Book of Moon and other Spells. LV8 requires its Summoning route and cannot be brought back with ordinary revival.
Dimension Fusion also returns the opponent's banished monsters. Mirage Dragon does not remove already-active Continuous Traps or protect you outside battle.

main_deck.name: Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest

thumbnail_strip: Green Baboon, Defender of the Forest

guide.summary: Turn recruiters into pressure, use battle tricks to preserve monsters, and manage the LP payments for Lily and Baboon.
game_plan: Use Rat and Momonga to maintain field presence; Momonga's LP gain helps fund Injection Fairy Lily and Green Baboon.
Apply pressure with a large attacker and protection. Rush Recklessly or Book of Moon can win a trade without spending another monster.
Banish expendable EARTH monsters for Gigantes or The Rock Spirit, creating a second threat after the opponent has used their main answer.
opening: A Set Rat lets you choose between more field presence, Injection Fairy Lily, or Exiled Force once you know the battle situation.
With Gorilla and protection, attack carefully; with Momonga and Creature Swap, prepare the exchange when the opponent can only give you a valuable monster.

Enraged Battle Ox grants piercing to your Beast, Beast-Warrior, and Winged Beast monsters; combine it with Gorilla to punish defenders.
Injection Fairy Lily can pay 2000 LP during damage calculation to overcome a boss; also account for Premature Burial's payment and Ring of Destruction's damage.
If a face-up Beast is destroyed by an effect and sent to the GY outside the Damage Step, Green Baboon can arrive from your hand or GY for 1000 LP.
pitfalls: Green Baboon cannot be Summoned following battle destruction within the Damage Step. Do not base its arrival on deliberately losing Rat or Momonga there.
Gorilla must attack if able and destroys itself in face-up Defense Position; Book of Moon only leaves it face-down temporarily.
Goblin Attack Force changes to Defense Position after attacking and is restricted from changing position; consider the next turn before leaving it exposed.
Gigantes destroyed by battle also wipes out your Spells and Traps. The Rock Spirit only gains its 300 ATK during the opponent's Battle Phase.

Use Hydrogeddon with Shrink, Book of Moon, and removal to destroy a monster by battle and summon another copy from the Deck.
Keep cards available to discard for Abyss Soldier and Frost and Flame Dragon; reaching the boss with no cards left for its effect reduces the value of the setup.
opening: A Set Crystal Seer or Mother Grizzly helps prepare WATER while defending. UFO Turtle finds the appropriate small FIRE monster if destroyed by battle.

key_plays: Mother Grizzly can access Crystal Seer, Sinister Serpent, or Yomi Ship; choose card advantage, discard material, or an answer to the attacker as needed.
Abyss Soldier discards a WATER monster to return a card to the hand, while also preparing part of Frost and Flame Dragon's Summoning cost.
Frost and Flame Dragon banishes two WATER monsters and one FIRE monster from your GY to summon itself, then can discard any card to destroy a monster.
Sylvan Hermitree summoned by Lonefire can attack as a large threat; its excavation only draws if it sends a Plant, so do not treat it as a guaranteed draw.
pitfalls: Frost and Flame Dragon cannot be revived with Premature Burial or Call of the Haunted; it requires its own procedure from the hand.

Abyss Soldier needs a WATER monster for its cost; spare FIRE monsters will not work. Frost and Flame Dragon is WATER and can be discarded, but avoid sacrificing your win condition without enough benefit.
Do not banish your only useful revival target for Frost without checking the follow-up. Lonefire and Sylvan Hermitree are FIRE; Crystal Seer is WATER.
Hydrogeddon must destroy a monster by battle and send it to the GY; it does not multiply by destroying Tokens or through your removal effects.

decks.description: Three Necrovalley, three Commandant, and Terraforming provide access to the Field Spell. Spy, Guard, and Assailant maintain the field while GY restrictions limit Chaos and revival routes.

guide.summary: Establish Necrovalley, build field presence with Spy, and turn your stat advantage into safe attacks.
game_plan: Search for Necrovalley when missing, and keep another way to find it after removal; do not spend every Commandant if you need attackers.
Protect Spy to summon the right Gravekeeper: another body, Guard for a future turn, or an attacker that benefits from the Field Spell.
Save Dust Tornado and Solemn Judgment for cards that dismantle Necrovalley or change the damage race, rather than answering every minor play.
opening: A Set Spy with Necrovalley and protection creates a 2500 DEF defender and threatens a second monster if flipped.
Commandant can search for Necrovalley or attack with 2100 ATK under it; decide based on whether the Field Spell is already available.
key_plays: Assailant changes a face-up opposing monster's battle position when declaring an attack with Necrovalley active; Spear Soldier adds piercing damage against defenders.
Tsukuyomi Sets Spy or Guard again so you can reuse its effect when it can be flipped once more.
Rite of Spirit revives a Gravekeeper despite Necrovalley. A Tribute Summoned Chief can bring back another and makes your GY unaffected by the Field Spell.
Assailant, Spear Soldier, Ambusher, or Chief under Necrovalley can pay for Deck Devastation Virus; confirm the chosen monster is still DARK and has at least 2000 ATK.

Spy searches for monsters with 1500 ATK or less in the Deck; Necrovalley does not increase their ATK there, and Commandant's 1600 ATK makes it ineligible.

Nobleman of Crossout on an opposing Spy or Guard can banish your copies from the Deck; Rite cannot help a monster that is already banished.

decks.description: Three Harpie Lady 1, three Harpie Queen, and two Harpie Oracle support Hunting Ground and Hysteric Party. Elegant Egotist extends your plays, and Swallow's Nest turns a Level 4 Winged Beast into the right piece.

game_plan: Search for Harpies' Hunting Ground with Queen when there is backrow to destroy; keep Queen as an attacker when the Field Spell would not have a useful target.
Develop your Harpies without spending the whole hand. Lady 1 boosts WIND monsters and helps smaller bodies compete in battle.
Prepare Hysteric Party with several Harpies in the GY and a card to discard so you can restore pressure after a board clear.
opening: Queen can search for Hunting Ground; with another Harpie ready to summon, activate the Field Spell first if there is a worthwhile target.

decks.title: HERO Fusion
decks.description: Fifteen different Fusions provide answers to a range of fields. Three E - Emergency Call, three King of the Swamp, and Prisma find or prepare materials for Polymerization, Miracle Fusion, and the two Future Fusion.

guide.summary: Choose the useful Fusion first, gather its exact materials, and save Miracle Fusion as a second wave.
game_plan: Use E - Emergency Call and Reinforcement of the Army to complete the play your hand actually supports: Prisma, a missing material, or a HERO that can battle.
Do not fuse just because you can. Gaia weakens a threat, Plasma Vice removes Attack Position monsters, and Wildedge punishes multiple monsters; choose for the field.
Build up materials through battles, Prisma, and Polymerization before spending Miracle Fusion, letting you present threats across more than one turn.
opening: King of the Swamp can search for Polymerization; first check whether you need to keep it in hand as a substitute for a named material.
Future Fusion must survive until your first Standby Phase to send materials. Opening with Woodsman and protection can prepare Polymerization for the following turn.
key_plays: Prisma reveals a Fusion and sends a material whose name is specifically listed on it; Prisma takes that name until the End Phase.
King of the Swamp substitutes for one specifically named material. For example, alongside Sparkman it can replace Flame Wingman for Shining Flare Wingman.
Miracle Fusion banishes materials from your field or GY; Gaia uses a HERO and an EARTH monster, while Nova Master uses a HERO and a FIRE monster.
Necroshade in the GY enables a Normal Summon without Tributes for a high-Level HERO such as Bladedge, once through that effect.
pitfalls: Royal Decree also negates your Mirror Force, Torrential Tribute, and Ring of Destruction; decide when to use those Traps before keeping Decree active.
Prisma cannot send a generic material just because the requirement says HERO, EARTH, or FIRE; King of the Swamp cannot substitute for generic requirements either.
Future Fusion is delayed, and Fusions that require a Fusion Summon cannot simply be recovered with Premature Burial.
Do not use Miracle to spend every material needed for another Fusion. Check for Necrovalley or an opposing Kycoo before planning to banish from the GY.

side_cards.reason: Removes fuel for opposing Chaos, Zombie and Fusion decks while preserving your graveyard for Miracle. As a Spell, it does not conflict with Decree.

side_cards.reason: An immediate, non-negatable answer to Necrovalley, Oppression, Drain or an attack lock. It opens a Fusion window without waiting for Dust and works under your own Decree. It only returns the card; it does not remove it permanently.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: For effect damage and burn. It is not HERO material, so it stays in the Side Deck until needed. Preserve E-Call, the Normal Monsters and the Fusion routes.

side_cards.name: Pulling the Rug
side_cards.reason: Monarchs and Gadgets gain advantage before Future pays off; Rug stops their Normal Summon trigger. Bringing it in together with Hero Blast requires removing Decree.

side_plans.note: Switch from Decree to interaction: Blast recovers Sparkman and removes Gadgets, while Rug answers Monarch. Do not use Blast as an answer to a 2400 ATK Monarch. Keep one Future Fusion and the entire Poly and Miracle engine.

guide.summary: Apply pressure with Normal Monsters, save ways to summon Metal Armored Bug, and evolve Ultimate Insect when you can protect it.
game_plan: Use Unexpected Dai on an empty field to summon Insect Knight, keeping your Normal Summon for a second monster or an answer.
Search for Metal Armored Bug with Summoner's Art only when you have Ancient Rules, Pinch Hopper, or a later revival route.
Evolve Ultimate Insect LV3 into LV5 and then LV7 during your Standby Phases; the Normal Monster plan keeps working while the chain develops.
opening: Dai before your Normal Summon lets you open with Knight plus a recruiter. Check whether the second monster justifies exposing yourself to mass removal.

key_plays: Ancient Rules summons Metal Armored Bug from the hand. Birthright brings Knight or Bug back from the GY to restore your attacking presence.
Insect Imitation can Tribute a Level 4 monster to summon Ultimate Insect LV5; this produces a large monster through a different route from its natural evolution.
Pinch Hopper sent from your field to the GY can summon an Insect from your hand, such as Metal Armored Bug, if its timing window is met.
LV5 summoned by LV3's effect reduces opposing ATK; LV7 summoned by LV5 reduces ATK and DEF. Protect the transition to gain those benefits.
pitfalls: The current list uses Nobleman of Crossout, not Foolish Burial. Do not assume you have a direct GY send that is no longer in the Main Deck.
Pinch Hopper has an optional 'when' effect: it can miss timing if its trip to the GY is not the last thing to happen, such as when Tributed as a cost.
LV5 summoned by Insect Imitation does not gain the ATK reduction associated with being summoned by LV3; the same applies to LV7 if it did not arrive through LV5.
Unexpected Dai requires an empty field and only summons a Level 4 or lower Normal Monster; Summoner's Art searches for Level 5 or higher Normal Monsters, so it cannot find Knight.

side_cards.reason: Against a repeated engine Spell (Future/Miracle/Ritual) or a Field Spell that has not resolved yet, a redundant Spell pays to negate, destroy and lock out the opponent's future copies. Do not use it if you must discard your only Ritual route.

side_cards.name: Seven Tools of the Bandit
side_cards.reason: Protects Ritual Summons and absorption against Trap activations without disabling Raigeki Break or Call. Costs 1000 LP and does not answer the effect of an already active Continuous Trap.

side_cards.name: Compulsory Evacuation Device
side_cards.reason: Against Fusion/Ritual/Chaos monsters or a monster you cannot absorb. A non-destruction answer; returning your own Relinquished requires another Ritual Summon, so it is not a free reset.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: Negates Chaos/Monarch/Harpie effects and protects Relinquished from removal by monster effects. Sinister can pay the cost, but the card still requires a discard.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Against burn while Relinquished limits attacks. Both Chaos copies come out in this plan so you do not need to support another engine alongside Ritual.

side_cards.name: Giant Trunade
side_cards.reason: Temporarily removes Necrovalley/Oppression/Drain and opens absorption/Ritual plays. It also returns cards equipped to Relinquished to their owners' hands; evaluate that before activating it.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Removes Spy/Guard/FLIP monsters without absorbing a low-ATK monster. Against an opposing Old Vindictive, it can banish yours from the Deck; keeping Tsukuyomi and Apprentice does not remove that caveat.

side_plans.note: Removes the entire three-Spellcaster slow recruiter package. Keeps all six LIGHT monsters and five Ritual searchers. Kycoo only removes GY cards when it deals damage, and its banishing restriction applies only to the opponent.

Removes the slow Flip package, not part of the Ritual engine. Cursed Seal requires a Spell discard and successful destruction to apply its lasting lock. Compulsory returns Fusion Monsters to the Extra Deck; it does not negate already activated effects.

Wrath negates the effect when it activates; Compulsory does not, so save it for another threat or to remove an attacker. Avoid routinely returning Gadgets. Do not combine this plan with another that removes the same three monsters.

Keeps Raigeki Break for interaction and keeps Call. Seven Tools answers activations; use Heavy/MST/Breaker/Trunade for an already active Continuous card. Trunade can return the monster equipped to Relinquished to the opponent's hand.

Three Relinquished, two Black Illusions, one ARA, two Raggeds and all searchers remain. Abandons Chaos under Necrovalley; Relinquished does not depend on the GY to absorb monsters. Seven Tools removes neither Necrovalley nor an already face-up Oppression.
A pure Ritual plan: Wombat covers effect damage, and Relinquished applies pressure without taking Ring's self-damaging trade. Save the LP payment for Seven Tools for an important piece.

decks.title: Spellcaster
decks.description: Three Apprentice Magician, Spy, and several Flip Effects maintain resources for Magical Dimension. Two Chaos Sorcerer, Chaos Command Magician, and Dark Magician of Chaos offer different ways to turn that development into pressure.

side_deck.name: Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell

guide.summary: Buy time with small Spellcasters, preserve your LIGHT monsters, and choose the moment to turn a body into a boss.
game_plan: Use Apprentice to access Crystal Seer or Old Vindictive Magician depending on whether you need to find cards or remove a monster.
Keep the list's six LIGHT monsters available as resources for Chaos; do not confuse the Spellcaster Type with the DARK Attribute.
Save Magical Dimension for a threat in hand and a situation where Tributing your monster and destroying another creates a clear improvement.
opening: A Set Apprentice or Spy plus protection lets you develop without committing a high-Level boss.
With a face-up Spellcaster, Magical Dimension, and Dark Magician of Chaos in hand, prepare the replacement when the opponent tries to remove your monster or when you can benefit from the destruction.
key_plays: Magical Dimension requires you to control a Spellcaster, Tributes your chosen monster, and summons a Spellcaster from your hand; afterward it can destroy a monster.
Dark Magician of Chaos recovers a Spell in the End Phase of the turn it was Summoned; protect its presence and choose the resource that makes your next turn useful.
Tsukuyomi Sets Spy, Guard, or a useful Flip monster again for later reuse.
Apprentice can place a counter on Breaker when it is a valid target, giving Breaker another way to remove backrow.
pitfalls: Dark Magician of Chaos does not recover a Spell immediately on Summon. If it leaves the field face-up, it is banished.
Magical Dimension needs a Spellcaster to activate and another summonable one in hand; it is not standalone removal with an empty hand.
Skilled Blue Magician supplies LIGHT and defense, but this list has no targets for its Summoning effect. Banishing it from the GY to place a counter also consumes a LIGHT monster that Chaos may need.
Chaos Command Magician does not protect your whole field: it negates monster effects that target only itself. Necrovalley and an opposing Kycoo can stop the Chaos plan.

side_cards.reason: Removes Field Spells and floodgates without Raigeki Break's discard and lets you Set a control Trap.

side_cards.name: Mind Crush
side_cards.reason: Punishes confirmed information from Gadget, Commandant, Harpie Queen, E - Emergency Call and Reinforcement of the Army.

side_cards.name: Nobleman of Crossout
side_cards.reason: Alongside the Main Deck copy, reaches three against Spy, Apprentice and Wall without exposing a Spellcaster to combat.

side_cards.name: Divine Wrath
side_cards.reason: A universal answer to monster effects; discarding LIGHT/DARK monsters prepares Chaos Sorcerer and revival plays.

side_cards.name: Cursed Seal of the Forbidden Spell

side_plans.note: Rug negates the effect activated on Normal Summon, Mind Crush uses the card revealed by Gadget, and Wrath covers effects outside that window. Keeps all six Main Deck LIGHT monsters to support both copies of Chaos Sorcerer.

side_plans.note: Renewal turns a small Spellcaster into removal plus a DARK Spellcaster, while Wrath prevents the monster engine from regaining tempo. None of the six LIGHT monsters for Chaos Sorcerer are cut.

side_plans.matchup: Chaos / Zombie / HERO / Dragon Future / Red-Eyes
side_plans.note: Kycoo prevents the opponent from banishing materials from the GYs without stopping your own Chaos plays; it does not block field materials. Save Cursed Seal for the repeated Spell that defines the opponent's engine during that Duel.
Dust avoids paying a discard to remove Field Spells, while Cursed Seal punishes the repeated Spell once you have identified it.
Three Noblemen including the Main Deck copy reduce the need to attack Spy, Apprentice, Crystal Seer or Set walls while keeping all six Main Deck LIGHT monsters for Chaos Sorcerer.

decks.title: Wall Rock
decks.description: Stone Statue of the Aztecs, Stronghold Guardian, and Cross Counter punish attacks into high DEF. Three Gear Golem the Moving Fortress and two Weapon Change offer an offensive route after stabilizing.

guide.summary: Make opposing attacks costly, protect the useful wall, and prepare a finish that does not depend on the opponent continuing to attack.
game_plan: Set an appropriate wall and keep Stronghold Guardian in hand to change a battle; do not reveal all your defensive options unnecessarily.
Use Golem Sentry and Guardian Sphinx to return threats to the hand instead of waiting indefinitely for attacks into your DEF.
Activate Weapon Change in advance and keep Gear Golem until your Standby Phase to turn its DEF into ATK and prepare direct damage.
opening: A Set Giant Rat can access Stone Statue or Gear Golem when destroyed by battle; remember that the recruited monster arrives in Attack Position.
A Set wall with Stronghold Guardian in hand and protection can punish the first attack; Des Lacooda must survive to produce draws through Flip Summons.
key_plays: Stronghold Guardian sends itself from the hand during the Damage Step to give the attacked defender 1500 DEF; with Stone Statue, this increases potential counterattack damage.
Cross Counter doubles battle damage when the defender's DEF exceeds the attacker's ATK, then destroys the attacker after damage calculation.
Weapon Change only acts during your Standby Phase: pay 700 and swap the ATK/DEF of a face-up Warrior or Machine. Gear Golem can go from 800 ATK/2200 DEF to 2200 ATK.
Gear Golem pays 800 LP in Main Phase 1 to attack directly. When Flip Summoned, Guardian Sphinx returns every opposing monster to the hand.
pitfalls: Weapon Change does not affect Stone Statue, which is a Rock, and does not swap stats immediately when you activate the Continuous Spell in the Main Phase.
Guardian Sphinx requires a Flip Summon for its return effect; being flipped face-up by an attack does not trigger it.
Staunch Defender needs your monster to be face-up; it cannot select a wall that is still Set. Waboku helps you survive but does not increase DEF or force the opponent to attack.
Defense does not cover effect damage or removal that avoids battle. Keep an offensive route available, and do not treat this themed list as an automatic lock-based win.

side_cards.name: My Body as a Shield
side_cards.reason: Protects your accumulated board from Smashing, Lightning Vortex, Torrential and other mass or targeted destruction.

side_cards.name: Disappear
side_cards.reason: Chained to Call, Premature or Book of Life, removes the GY target and makes the relevant revival fail.

side_cards.name: Des Wombat
side_cards.reason: Covers a defensive strategy's natural weakness to Solar Flare, Volcanic Slicer, Ring and other damage sources that do not need to attack.

side_plans.note: Guardian Sphinx comes out because Mask of Restrict would prevent its Tribute Summon. Pulling the Rug answers Gadget and Monarch effects activated on Normal Summon.
Disappear removes the GY target in the Chain, while Dust removes Call of the Mummy, Premature, Call or Future Fusion.
Shield Crush removes defenders without flipping them; Limiter Removal gives Gear Golem a damage route once the game is stabilized.
My Body protects the walls from destruction, while Dust forces the opponent to respond before accumulating backrow.
Wombat stops damage that bypasses combat, while Dust removes Molten Destruction or Continuous cards before the finish.

decks.title: Zombie
decks.description: Two Gozuki, two Goblin Zombie, and two Foolish Burial prepare the GY. Call of the Mummy puts large monsters into play from the hand, while Book of Life brings them back and removes an opposing monster.

guide.summary: Prepare useful revival targets, use Goblin Zombie's searches, and present large threats in successive waves.
game_plan: Use Gozuki or Foolish Burial to send a Zombie you can use soon: a boss for revival, or Gozuki to enable a Summon from the hand.
Use Call of the Mummy before developing other monsters; your Normal Summon can then add Gozuki, Goblin Zombie, or an attacker.
Save Book of Life to recover a relevant monster and banish an opposing piece; always keep the targets in both GYs in mind.
opening: With Call of the Mummy and Ryu Kokki, Despair from the Dark, or Vampire Lord, summon from the hand first while your field is empty.
Gozuki plus Book of Life can set up revival when the opponent already has a monster in the GY; if they do not, hold Book.
key_plays: Goblin Zombie searches for a Zombie with 1200 DEF or less when sent from the field to the GY; Gozuki, another Goblin Zombie, Spirit Reaper, Des Lacooda, and Master Kyonshee are this list's options.
Gozuki sent to the GY can banish another Zombie other than Gozuki to summon a Zombie from the hand; preserve that cost as well as the threat.
Creature Swap can give away Goblin Zombie; if it later goes from the field to your GY, its search replaces a piece.

Ryu Kokki punishes Warriors and Spellcasters after battling. When Vampire Lord deals battle damage, you declare Monster, Spell, or Trap and the opponent sends a card of that type from their Deck to the GY; it can also return after being destroyed by an opposing effect.
pitfalls: There is no Pyramid Turtle in this Main Deck. Goblin Zombie can search for Gozuki with 800 DEF, but not Ryu Kokki with 2000 DEF or Vampire Lord with 1500 DEF.
Call of the Mummy requires you to still control no monsters when its effect resolves; do not chain your own development that would invalidate this condition.
Book of Life needs your Zombie and an opposing monster in their respective GYs to activate; having only your own target is not enough.
Regenerating Mummy and Despair from the Dark respond to an opposing effect sending them from the hand; your own discards do not grant those benefits.
